ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Aegean Architecture (Minoan and Mycenaean)
n: Knossos represents the earlier, largely unfortified Minoan palace tradition on Crete, while Mycenae and Tiryns are fortified Mycenaean citadels on the Greek mainland.

q: The temple city of Angkor, begun in the 1100s, is located in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Southeast Asian Architecture
n: Angkor, begun in the 1100s, is in Cambodia and represents the peak of Khmer temple architecture.

q: The Farnese Palace in Rome (1530s) was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Renaissance Architecture
n: Antonio da Sangallo the Younger (1484–1546) designed the Farnese Palace beginning in the 1530s.

q: The Treasury of the Siphnians was built at which sanctuary?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Greek Architecture
n: The Siphnian Treasury (c. 530 BC) stood at Delphi, sanctuary of Apollo, and is known for its caryatid porch.

q: The ceremonial center at Tikal, in Guatemala, was built by which culture?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Mesoamerican Architecture
n: Tikal (AD 400s–700s) in Guatemala was a major Maya ceremonial center.

q: San Giorgio Maggiore in Venice, designed by Palladio, dates to roughly:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Renaissance Architecture
n: Palladio designed San Giorgio Maggiore in the 1560s–1570s.

q: The Temple of Athena Pronaia is located at:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Greek Architecture
n: This temple (c. 400 BC) stood at Delphi, dedicated to Athena as guardian "before the temple" of Apollo.

q: Machu Picchu, the mountaintop Inca citadel, was built in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Mesoamerican Architecture
n: Machu Picchu (1450–1530) is in Peru, built by the Inca.

q: The New Sacristy at San Lorenzo, Florence, housing Medici tombs, was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Mannerism
n: Michelangelo designed the New Sacristy at San Lorenzo in the 1520s.

q: The Temple of the Olympian Zeus in Athens was finally completed in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Greek Architecture
n: Though begun centuries earlier, the temple was only completed under Emperor Hadrian in AD 132.

q: Cahokia, the largest pre-Columbian settlement north of Mexico, was located near:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Native American Architecture
n: Cahokia (c. 1150) was a major mound-building center near East St. Louis, Missouri.

q: Arden House, an example of English Tudor style, is located in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Tudor Style
n: Arden House (early 1500s) is in Stratford-Upon-Avon.

q: The Porta Augusta, an Etruscan city gate later reused in Roman construction, stands at:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Etruscan Architecture
n: The Porta Augusta (c. 100s BC) is an Etruscan gate in Perugia.

q: San Vitale, known for its Byzantine mosaics, is located in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Byzantine Architecture
n: San Vitale (AD 546) is in Ravenna, Italy, and features famous mosaics of Justinian and Theodora.

q: Versailles Palace, built in the 1660s, involved which architects?
o: Francois Mansart, Louis Le Vau, and Jules Hardouin-Mansart
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Baroque Architecture
n: Versailles Palace was developed by Francois Mansart (1598–1666), Louis Le Vau (1612–1670), and Jules Hardouin-Mansart.

q: The Ara Pacis (Altar of Peace) was dedicated in Rome in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Roman Architecture
n: Augustus's Ara Pacis was completed in 13 BC to commemorate peace after his military campaigns.

q: The Cathedral of San Marco, with its Byzantine-influenced domes, is located in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 25 — Byzantine Architecture
n: The Cathedral of San Marco (1063) in Venice, Italy, shows strong Byzantine architectural influence.

q: The Town Hall of Amsterdam, built 1648–1655, was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Baroque Architecture
n: Jacob van Campen (with Pieter Post) designed Amsterdam's Town Hall, completed in 1655.

q: The Arch of Titus in Rome, commemorating the sack of Jerusalem, was completed in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Roman Architecture
n: The Arch of Titus was dedicated in AD 81, after Titus's death, honoring his victories including the destruction of the Second Temple.

q: The Great Mosque of Cordoba, Spain, was begun in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 25 — Islamic Architecture (Moorish, Mughal, Ottoman, Seljuk)
n: The Great Mosque of Cordoba was begun in 785 under Abd al-Rahman I.

q: San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane in Rome, built 1630s–1665, was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Baroque Architecture
n: Francesco Borromini (1599–1667) designed San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane, known for its undulating facade.

q: The Column of Trajan, commemorating the Dacian Wars, was erected in Rome in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Roman Architecture
n: Trajan's Column was dedicated in AD 113, its spiral relief narrating the Dacian campaigns.

q: The Selimiye Mosque in Edirne, Turkey (1570s), considered its architect's masterpiece, was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 25 — Islamic Architecture (Moorish, Mughal, Ottoman, Seljuk)
n: The great Ottoman architect Sinan designed the Selimiye Mosque, widely regarded as his finest work.

q: Blenheim Palace in Woodstock, England (1705), was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Baroque Architecture
n: John Vanbrugh (1664–1726) designed Blenheim Palace, completed in 1705.

q: Hadrian's Wall, marking the northern frontier of Roman Britain, dates to:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Roman Architecture
n: Hadrian's Wall, begun under Hadrian and maintained afterward, is dated in the reviewer to the AD 200s, across northern Great Britain.

q: The Suleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul (1550s) was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 25 — Islamic Architecture (Moorish, Mughal, Ottoman, Seljuk)
n: The Suleymaniye Mosque was designed by the great Ottoman architect Sinan (Mimar Koca Agha, 1489–1588).

q: The Salon de la Princesse at the Hotel de Soubise in Paris (1732) was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Rococo Architecture
n: Germain Boffrand (1667–1754) designed the Salon de la Princesse in 1732, a celebrated Rococo interior.

q: The Basilica of Maxentius and Constantine, the largest Roman basilica, was completed in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Roman Architecture
n: Completed around AD 310, it was started under Maxentius and finished after Constantine's victory over him.

q: Charlemagne's Palace Complex at Aachen, Germany (792–805), exemplifies which architectural style?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 25 — Early Medieval Architecture (Carolingian and Ottonian)
n: Charlemagne's Palace Complex at Aachen is a hallmark of Carolingian architecture, drawing on Roman and Byzantine models.

q: Vierzehnheiligen, a pilgrimage church at Staffelstein, Germany (1743), was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Rococo Architecture
n: Johann Balthasar Neumann designed Vierzehnheiligen, completed in 1743.

q: The House-Church at Dura-Europos, one of the earliest known Christian worship spaces, is located in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Early Semitic and Christian Architecture
n: The Dura-Europos house-church (AD 240s) in Syria is among the oldest identified Christian meeting places.

q: The Church of Saint Cyriakus at Gernrode, Germany, begun in 961, belongs to which style?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 25 — Early Medieval Architecture (Carolingian and Ottonian)
n: Begun in 961, this church at Gernrode is an example of Ottonian architecture.

q: Catherine Palace at Tsarskoye Selo, outside St. Petersburg (1752–1756), was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Rococo Architecture
n: Rastrelli designed Catherine Palace, completed in 1756.

q: Santa Sabina, noted for its early basilica form and carved wooden doors, was built in Rome in the:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Early Semitic and Christian Architecture
n: Santa Sabina dates to the AD 420s and is one of the best-preserved early Christian basilicas.

q: The Pisa Cathedral Complex, including its famous leaning tower, is located in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 25 — Romanesque Architecture; see also Castle
n: The Pisa Cathedral Complex, begun in the 1060s, is in Italy.

q: The Radcliffe Camera in Oxford (1739–1749) is associated with the architect:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Neo-Classical Architecture
n: James Gibbs designed the Radcliffe Camera, completed in 1749, one of England's earliest circular libraries.

q: Mohenjo-Daro, one of the great early Indus Valley cities, dates to roughly:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Indian Architecture
n: Mohenjo-Daro, one of the largest Bronze Age Indus Valley cities, dates to about 2600 BC.

q: The Tower of London was begun in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 25 — Romanesque Architecture; see also Castle
n: The Tower of London was begun in 1078 under William the Conqueror.

q: The Neolithic village of Catal Huyuk, dated to roughly 6500 BC, is located in which present-day country?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Prehistoric Architecture (Paleolithic and Neolithic)
n: Catal Huyuk, one of the earliest large farming settlements, sits in south-central Turkey.

q: The Rock-Cut Hall of Karla, a Buddhist chaitya (assembly hall), dates to roughly:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Indian Architecture
n: The Rock-Cut Hall at Karla dates to about 100s BC.

q: The Cathedral of Saint-Lazare, begun in the 1130s, is located at:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 25 — Romanesque Architecture; see also Castle
n: The Cathedral of Saint-Lazare is in Autun, France, a Romanesque church famed for its sculpted tympanum.

q: The Neolithic passage tombs of Newgrange are located in which country?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Prehistoric Architecture (Paleolithic and Neolithic)
n: Newgrange, dated c. 3000–2500 BC, is a passage tomb complex in Ireland.

q: The Rajarajeshvara Temple to Shiva was built at:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Indian Architecture
n: The Rajarajeshvara Temple (c. 1000) stands at Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, a major monument of Chola-dynasty temple architecture.

q: Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris dates to roughly:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 25 — Gothic Architecture
n: Notre Dame de Paris dates to the 1160s in its initial construction.

q: Jericho's famous city walls, among the earliest known defensive walls, date to roughly what period?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Near Eastern Architecture
n: Jericho's stone walls and tower date to about 7000 BC, making them some of the earliest urban fortifications known.

q: Chang'an, capital of the Tang Dynasty, flourished during:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Chinese Architecture
n: Chang'an was the capital of the Tang Dynasty, which ruled AD 618–907.

q: Cologne Cathedral, one of the tallest Gothic cathedrals, is located in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 25 — Gothic Architecture
n: Cologne Cathedral (1240s) is in Germany.

q: The Temple of Solomon stood in which city?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Near Eastern Architecture
n: Solomon's Temple was built in Jerusalem, with a history running from roughly the late 900s BC until its final destruction in AD 70.

q: The Forbidden City in Beijing was built under which dynasty?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Chinese Architecture
n: The Forbidden City (1368–1644) was the imperial palace complex of the Ming Dynasty.

q: The dome of Florence Cathedral, a defining engineering feat of the early Renaissance, was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Renaissance Architecture
n: Filippo Brunelleschi (c. 1377–1446) engineered Florence Cathedral's dome in the 1420s without traditional wooden centering.

q: Darius I's palace complex at Persepolis dates to roughly which period?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Near Eastern Architecture
n: Construction at Persepolis, ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Persian empire, ran from about 518 to 460 BC under Darius I and his successors.

q: The Jin Mao Building in Shanghai (1998) was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Chinese Architecture
n: The Jin Mao Building (1998) in Shanghai was designed by the firm Skidmore, Owings & Merrill.

q: Santo Spirito in Florence, designed on a strict grid of proportions, dates to roughly:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Renaissance Architecture
n: Santo Spirito, another Brunelleschi church in Florence, dates to the 1430s.

q: The wooden models depicting daily life from the Tomb of Meketra were found at:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Egyptian Architecture
n: The Meketra tomb models (c. 2100 BC) were discovered at Thebes.

q: Byodo-in, a Heian-period temple known for its Phoenix Hall, is located at:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Japanese Architecture
n: Byodo-in (c. 1053, Heian Period) stands at Uji in Kyoto Prefecture.

q: The Tempio Malatestiano in Rimini was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Renaissance Architecture
n: Leon Battista Alberti (1404–1472) designed the Tempio Malatestiano in Rimini in the 1450s.

q: The Temple of Amun, Mut, and Khonsu was built at:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Egyptian Architecture
n: This temple complex (c. 1279 BC) is at Luxor, linked to Karnak by an avenue of sphinxes.

q: The Yoyogi Gymnasium, built for the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Japanese Architecture
n: Kenzo Tange (1913–2005) designed the Yoyogi National Gymnasium for the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

q: Santa Maria delle Carceri in Prato, Italy (1485), was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Renaissance Architecture
n: Giuliano da Sangallo designed Santa Maria delle Carceri in Prato in 1485.

q: The Citadel at Mycenae, fortified with massive stone walls, is located in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Aegean Architecture (Minoan and Mycenaean)
n: Mycenae (c. 1600–1200 BC), the citadel that gave Mycenaean civilization its name, is on the Greek mainland.

q: The Church of the Light (1989), known for its cruciform wall slit, was designed by Tadao Ando in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Japanese Architecture
n: Ando's Church of the Light (1989) is located in Ibaraki-shi, Osaka.

q: Michelangelo took over design of the dome of Saint Peter's Church in Rome during roughly which period?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Renaissance Architecture
n: Michelangelo directed work on Saint Peter's, including its dome, from the 1530s into the 1560s.

q: The Temple of Hera I, an early Doric temple, was built at:
ref: x
n: Wait

q: La Venta, with its Great Pyramid and ballcourt, was built by which culture?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Mesoamerican Architecture
n: La Venta (c. 900–600 BC) in Mexico was an Olmec ceremonial center.

q: The Library building in Venice (1520s) was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Renaissance Architecture
n: Jacopo Sansovino (1486–1570) designed the Library in Venice in the 1520s.

q: The Acropolis of Athens, including the Parthenon, was largely built in which period?
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 23 — Ancient Greek Architecture
n: Most of the Acropolis's major buildings date to the mid-400s BC, under Pericles's building program.

q: Chichen Itza, a major Maya city, is located in:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 24 — Mesoamerican Architecture
n: Chichen Itza (800s–1200s) is in the Yucatan region of Mexico.

q: The Teatro Olimpico in Vicenza, completed with Vincenzo Scamozzi, was designed by:
ref: History of Architecture Tables, p. 26 — Renaissance Architecture
n: Palladio designed the Teatro Olimpico (1580s–1585), one of the earliest surviving indoor theaters, completed after his death with Vincenzo Scamozzi's help.
